acceptance: Persistent task state (JSON records in git) with explicit valid transitions; completed is terminal
Stable task and execution identifiers (task id + run id per attempt)
Idempotency and duplicate-execution protection (claimSideEffect; PR-exists check before creating PRs)
An append-only record of state changes and execution outcomes (events.jsonl, never rewritten)
Detection of interrupted work (reconciler: open run with no terminal event, including crash-before-task_started)
Bounded retries with backoff (max 3 attempts; exhaustion blocks the task with a recorded reason)
Safe recovery after a process restart (reconcile CLI; idempotent re-runs change nothing)
Reconciliation when an external operation succeeds but local recording fails (pre-checks before side effects; task-files-before-events write order leaves recovery, never stuck state)
Isolation of blocked tasks so independent work continues (reconciler leaves blocked/queued/completed tasks untouched)
Automated tests for interruption, duplicate submissions, invalid transitions, retry exhaustion, and recovery after restart

Orchestrator reconcile smoke test on the live repo: '1 tasks, 0 changed, 0 events appended', no stray files created

Orchestrator review catch fixed in the second attempt: interruption detection no longer depends on a task_started event existing (crash-before-event case now covered by its own test)
Demo task file untouched (diff grep count 0); technology decision recorded in docs/durable-execution.md (JSON-in-git over SQLite/Postgres/engines, with revisit triggers)
objective: Establish the minimum durable execution layer for Genesis before any unattended testing: persistent task state, a state machine, stable identifiers, idempotency, an append-only event record, interruption detection, bounded retries, restart recovery, and blocked-task isolation — using only files in git, no new database, engine, or paid service.
